criterion_notes.c1: Examines government provision of rural safe drinking water infrastructure to villages and schools across 82 counties in Guizhou Province under China's National Rural Drinking Water Safety Project (2010–2013).
criterion_notes.c2: Passes the plain wording of Criterion 2 (plain_criterion2_decision = 'include') because it examines formal institutional and governance factors—specifically regional ethnic autonomy status (Autonomous County and Autonomous Prefecture designations), county political/administrative leadership ethnicity (Share Han Leaders, alongside minority-governor reservation rules), and decentralized bureaucratic implementation discretion in siting water projects. However, it fails the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading of Criterion 2 (decision = 'exclude', exclusion_code = 'E03'): the primary independent variable is county ethnic demographic composition (Percentage Minority / Diversity), and the institutional variables tested capture macro-territorial ethnic autonomy and co-ethnic distributive politics in upstream intergovernmental capital-project allocation across counties. Although the author qualitatively invokes local officials' discretion under short cadre evaluation timelines, discretion is unmeasured in the empirical models and concerns generic infrastructure project delivery/siting (choosing easier Han-majority areas to complete construction quickly) rather than a rule-type legal, regulatory, or administrative mechanism directly governing household or community service access (such as eligibility screening, documentation/tenure rules, tariffs, enforcement, or street-level accommodation of access rules).
criterion_notes.c3: Empirical mixed-methods study combining county-level OLS and multilevel regressions on internal provincial Ministry of Water Resources records covering 13,376 rural drinking water projects (2010–2013), 2010 census data, and biographical data on 360 county officials with qualitative field visits to over 50 villages and interviews.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports cumulative county-level counts of MWR drinking water project beneficiaries (villagers and students served by completed projects) and project funding (RMB), which capture community drinking-water infrastructure availability/provision, though the author notes that follow-up household water access outcomes after construction are not directly measured.
criterion_notes.c5: Clearly identifies the population and unit of analysis (82 counties in Guizhou Province, China; N = 61 counties in full regression models, aggregated from 13,376 MWR projects), exposures (county percentage minority, diversity, autonomous county/prefecture status, and share of Han county leaders), outcomes (project beneficiaries and project funds per county), and observational regression study design.

evidence_quotes.quote: I draw on interviews and a new data set of over 10,000 drinking water projects funded by the Ministry of Water Resources (MWR) in rural areas of Guizhou Province in southwest China.

Information about community needs and local implementation efforts pass through the same channels, so there is room for discretion in prioritizing where facilities should be built (Shou 2015; Zhao 2013).

Model 1 shows that fewer individuals beneﬁt from projects when a larger share of the population is from ethnic-minority groups. This simple model shows that government allocations disproportionately favor Han areas. Model 2 adds controls for the two main alternative explanations: county autonomy and co-ethnic leaders.
The key outcome I explore is the beneﬁciaries, that is the number of people who beneﬁt from government water projects. Secondarily, I look at the amount of funding counties receive.
While the government infrastructure is a key component of drinking water provision, more research is needed to directly assess water access outcomes.

raw_response.exposure: County ethnic minority population share (percentage minority) and ethnic diversity; regional minority autonomous county and prefecture status; and ethnicity of county governors and CCP Party secretaries (share Han leaders)
raw_response.outcome: Cumulative number of beneficiaries (villagers and students) of completed Ministry of Water Resources rural safe drinking water infrastructure projects per county (2010–2013) and total MWR project funds (RMB) per county
raw_response.population_and_sample: Rural counties in Guizhou Province, southwest China (82 counties total, N = 61 counties in main regression models; aggregated from 13,376 Ministry of Water Resources rural drinking water projects authorized in 2010–2013, alongside 360 county governors and CCP Party secretaries and field visits to over 50 villages)
raw_response.rationale: Excluded under E03 (Wrong exposure) per the 2026-10-13 Criterion 2 clarification. While the study empirically examines rural drinking water infrastructure allocation across 82 counties in Guizhou Province and would be included under the broad/plain wording of Criterion 2 (plain_criterion2_decision = 'include') because it tests regional ethnic autonomy status, co-ethnic county leadership, and discusses decentralized implementation discretion, its exposures are ethnic demographics, co-ethnic political representation, and macro-territorial autonomy in upstream public-goods capital project allocation/delivery rather than a rule-type legal, regulatory, or administrative mechanism directly governing last-mile water service access.
raw_response.study_design: Observational cross-sectional county-level regression analysis (OLS and multilevel models) of administrative project records, supplemented by qualitative field observations and interviews
